verdict.rationale: SigNoz's GitHub README states that the free open-source SigNoz runs in your own infrastructure via Docker, Kubernetes, or Linux, with full control of the data plane. Community users discuss running the self-hosted stack, and their complaints about container count, a failed Windows install, and the separately licensed ee/ directory are caveats rather than contradictions. missing for 10: in-depth first-party self-hosting install/operations docs in the evidence, clarity on which ee/-licensed features are excluded from the self-hosted open-source edition, lighter-weight or Windows-supported deployment path.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Free open-source SigNoz that runs in your own infrastructure. Deploy with Docker, Kubernetes, or Linux and keep full control of your data plane.
says SigNoz looks easy to add to Kubernetes
